header: How four readers use the open data
lead: The series is public, so the institute is rarely the first to notice what it shows. These readers told us what they do with it.

quotes.quote_text: The annual report used to tell us what the river had done. Now we read the same day's numbers and plan our discharge around them.
quotes.author: Peter Sonnleitner

image.alternative: A woman in her thirties with dark hair tied back and a navy polo shirt.

quotes.quote_text: My students download the July series themselves and argue about the outliers. That argument is the lesson. A table in a textbook could never start it.
quotes.author: Miriam Kaltner

image.alternative: A man in his sixties with glasses and a navy cardigan.

quotes.quote_text: Before a permit hearing, I check the two stations on either side of the outfall. It takes four minutes and has twice changed what we ask for.
quotes.author: Andrej Lubic

image.alternative: A woman in her forties with shoulder-length brown hair and a navy jumper.

quotes.quote_text: We trust the checked data because the raw data is published too. Seeing what was removed is worth more than being told the result is reliable.
quotes.author: Dr. Feline Oberkirch
quotes.role: Hydrology group, Talhof university of applied sciences

image.alternative: A bald man in his forties wearing a high-visibility jacket.
